title: Using CBT-style skills to re-engage cognitive work
preferred_framing: channel emotional arousal into reflective and executive processing
avoid_framing: move emotion into the prefrontal cortex
evidence_scope: The neuroscience cited here is laboratory human neuroimaging evidence about affect labelling and cognitive reappraisal. It does not directly test coding, academic study, debugging, writing performance, clinical outcomes, or this five-step workflow as a package.
mechanism_summary: in a 2007 fMRI study of 30 participants aged 18–36 performing affect-labelling tasks on emotional facial stimuli, affect labelling was associated with increased right ventrolateral prefrontal activity and reduced amygdala/limbic responding relative to comparison conditions

a 2014 meta-analysis of 48 human neuroimaging studies, mostly involving downregulation of negative affect, found consistent recruitment of cognitive-control and lateral temporal regions with modulation of bilateral amygdala activity during reappraisal

these laboratory findings support possible regulation mechanisms but do not establish that the same neural pattern occurs during coding or study, that the cited samples represent every population, or that a specific exercise will improve performance or provide any productivity guarantee

workflow.prompt: Name the emotion or state precisely enough to work with it: frustrated, anxious, embarrassed, overloaded, stuck.
Write the observable problem separately from the prediction or judgement attached to it.
Generate a more balanced interpretation that preserves the facts without adding catastrophe.
Choose the smallest concrete next action that produces information.
Do that action, then review what actually happened before choosing the next step.

examples.coding: The tests are failing → I am frustrated → 'I have broken everything' is a prediction → run the smallest failing test and inspect the first changed invariant.
examples.academic: The paper feels impossible → I am overwhelmed → separate 'I do not yet understand section 3' from 'I cannot understand this' → define one question and read only for that answer.
examples.writing: The draft feels bad → embarrassment is present → distinguish quality judgement from the observable editing problem → revise one paragraph or argument edge.

guardrails: rest sleep food medical care accessibility changes collaboration or stepping away may be the correct next action
do not use this framework to moralise productivity
persistent or severe distress deserves appropriate support even if work can still be completed
mechanistic neuroscience claims remain evidence_supported rather than guaranteed individual effects
do not generalise laboratory neuroimaging findings into claims about real-world cognitive-work performance without direct evidence
